Q: Target "unknown" in Android device chooser in Eclipse A:

The problem for me turned out to be insufficient rights of the ADB server.

I run Android Studio through Remote Desktop (I used a laptop to connect to a local, more powerful computer). Apparently, I didn't have all the privileges when running through Remote Desktop.

After stopping the ADB server and restarting it with root privileges, it solved the problem.

sudo ./adb kill-server
sudo ./adb root

It turns out I had to do this just the first time. Since the first time I don't have to do this anymore.

Q: How do I get started coding HTML Applications (HTA) for game development A:

To add to what @LesFerch said: since MS is deprecating VBScript, you could also choose JScript (the dialect of ECMA Script that's only a bit different from the everpresent JavaScript) in your HTA code.

My suggestion would be to select some existing HTA project that looks attractive to you, and then start removing the code down to the bare bones.

I did something similar to what you aim in my attempt to write a NullSoft Installer clone: https://github.com/sskras/installer.hta#initial-try

There is a short essay about my motivation, which I find being similar to yours. It took me a couple of month to do 186 commits for this Proof-of-Concept, and the result looks like that:

The project is unfinished yet.

I also must warn that to run HTAs on modern Windows flawlessly it requires quite a bunch of hacks. I have implemented only a part of them. Please see some of the open repo issues.

Or if the project is open source (like mine), you could easily follow their development from the initial commit till the end.

Cheers!

Q: I am learning Python and I am confused about string comparison logic. I wrote this code: A:

You only care about the rest of the string when the first characters are equal. str.__le__ looks something like

def __le__(s1, s2):
    if s1 == "":
        # "" <= any string
        return True
    elif s2 == "":
        # x <= "" is False for any nonempty string
        return False
    elif s1[0] == s2[0]
        # First characters are equal, compare the remaining characters recursively.
        return s1[1:] <= s2[1:]
    else:
        # Otherwise, the first characters are sufficient and the rest can be ignored
        return s1[0] <= s2[0]

Q: How to incrementally merge daily CSV delta updates into a master file without losing expired records? A:

You likely want to construct a dictionary with a key of the booking id when reading your master CSV. That way, as you process each transaction from your delta file you will be able to find the corresponding master record quickly. An even better solution might be to maintain the master dataset in a proper database with indexes. You can always reproduce the master in some other format when needed.
